name: Aspergillus niger prolyl endopeptidase (AN-PEP)
short: Coeliac pilot, 16 adults ate gluten with the enzyme (no placebo group described in this phase): 2 had gut-lining damage worsen by two Marsh steps in 2 weeks; no serious adverse events or withdrawals.
text: In a pilot study, 16 adults with coeliac disease whose gut lining had healed on a strict gluten-free diet ate toast containing about 7 g of gluten a day together with the enzyme for 2 weeks (a safety phase, for which the abstract describes no placebo group; 14 of them were then randomized to gluten with either the enzyme or placebo, and the abstract calls the study as a whole randomised, double-blind and placebo-controlled). Two of them were not continued into the next phase because their duodenal biopsies showed an increase of two Marsh steps (worsening gut-lining damage) after those 2 weeks, even though their blood antibody tests stayed undetectable. No serious adverse events occurred and no one withdrew, and the authors describe the enzyme as appearing well tolerated; however, the trial's main comparison could not show an effect because the placebo group did not deteriorate on gluten either. No interaction data were found in the cited source.
